title: DNA content of onion root tip cells
body: A student stained nuclei of actively dividing onion root tip cells (2n = 16) and measured the relative amount of DNA in each nucleus. Taking the DNA content of a nucleus just after cytokinesis as 2C, the cells fell into three groups. Group X nuclei had 2C, Group Y nuclei had values spread between 2C and 4C, and Group Z nuclei had 4C. Very few cells showed visible condensed chromosomes; most nuclei looked like interphase nuclei with a distinct nucleolus.
